questions.title: Design a high-performance Autocomplete / Typeahead widget.
questions.description:
Autocomplete Widget Design

Designing an autocomplete component tests UI API design, optimization skills, network request handling, and accessibility.

Key Architectural Pillars

  • Network Optimization: Debounce keyboard inputs to prevent firing API queries on every keystroke. Cache previous queries in-memory.
  • State Management: Cache key-value pairs (query to results). Support loading and empty states.
  • Keyboard Navigation: Use arrow keys to select items, Escape to close list, Enter to confirm, and tab indexing.
  • Aria Role Specifications: Combobox role, listbox role for dropdown, and aria-autocomplete="list".
questions.bestPractices:
• Limit results in the view to 5-10 items.
  • Use a Trie data structure on the client or server for prefix matching.
  • Support offline search using stored values when network is unavailable.
questions.commonMistakes:
• Firing API requests on every single keypress, overloading servers.
  • Race conditions: returning older results after newer searches due to fast typists. (Use abort controllers to cancel previous request).
questions.example:
// Simple race-condition proof fetch effect
useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  
  const fetchData = async () => {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/search?q=${query}`, {
        signal: controller.signal
      });
      const data = await res.json();
      setResults(data);
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.name !== 'AbortError') handleErrors(err);
    }
  };

  if (query) fetchData();
  return () => controller.abort(); // Cancel if query changes
}, [query]);
questions.interviewTip: Draw out the layout and API payload structure. Discuss debounce timers (e.g. 300ms) and how aborting stale requests with AbortController prevents out-of-order rendering updates (race conditions).
